title: Breast Lift Cost in 2026: What You Pay and What to Ask
meta_description: The ASPS average is $6,816, before anesthesia and facility costs. See Alluring's prices with and without implants, what a quote should list, and insurance.
excerpt: The average breast lift cost you see quoted is only part of the total. Here is what that figure leaves out, Alluring's prices with and without implants, what a quote should spell out, what moves the price, insurance, financing and how to compare quotes.
quick_answer:
How much does a breast lift cost?

The American Society of Plastic Surgeons puts the average cost of a breast lift at $6,816, which does not include anesthesia, operating room facilities or other related expenses. Your total also depends on the surgeon, the technique, the location and any implants. The society says most health insurance plans don't cover it.

sources.title: How much does a breast lift cost?
quotes: The average cost of a breast lift (mastopexy) is $6,816 , according to the latest statistics from the American Society of Plastic Surgeons.
This average cost is only part of the total price – it does not include anesthesia, operating room facilities or other related expenses.
A surgeon's fee for breast lift surgery will be based on his or her experience, the type of procedure used and the geographic office location.
Most health insurance plans do not cover breast lift surgery or its complications, but many plastic surgeons offer patient financing plans, so be sure to ask.
Hospital or surgical facility costs
Prescriptions for medication

When choosing a board-certified plastic surgeon in your area for a breast lift, remember that the surgeon's experience and your comfort with him or her are just as important as the final cost of the surgery.

notes: New post under the 2026-11-03 brief (post 5). All prices are on the facts file. No regional range: none found from a qualifying source, and the post says so. The Aesthetic Society's average is described without its figure (facts file: never beside the ASPS figure; check_post fails any dollar figure off the facts file). The combination discount is worded for a lift WITHOUT implants, since the brief bars applying it to a lift with implants. Not stated, because they are owner questions: what Alluring's prices include, which incision each price covers, where surgery is done, whether the list prices are before or after the sheet's handwritten 20% off. Added beyond the brief, each from a government source read in this session: the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act exception (DOL), medical credit card terms with no numbers (CFPB), and the HSA and FSA question (IRS 502 and 969). Mayo Clinic and CareCredit are not used. '2026' is in the title because prices are year-specific; the ASPS figure carries no year. Fact-check round, 3 Nov: title now 'What to Ask'; the ASPS average no longer says 'surgeon's fee' or 'national'; WHCRA, HSA and FSA and time-off wording tightened. The CFPB paragraph stays.
